sub_answers.sub_question: What are the dominant experimental systematic uncertainties reported by ATLAS for B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios?
How do uncertainties in B-meson production fractions and fragmentation affect ATLAS branching ratio determinations?
sub_answers.text:
Uncertainties in the measured pT spectrum of the parent b hadron affect derived branching fractions through a pt-dependent acceptance correction [d141416s0p0].
External uncertainties on measured branching ratios used for normalization propagate into the final branching-fraction determinations [d141416s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What theoretical inputs (e.g., decay constants, form factors) and their uncertainties enter the interpretation of B→μμ results?
sub_answers.text:
Decay constants and transition form factors are key theoretical inputs for heavy-to-light and semileptonic B decays and are computed within models such as the covariant light-front quark model [d10721s0p0].
Those form factors and decay constants have sensitivity to hadronic model parameters (for example the wave-function parameter beta) and associated uncertainties enter predictions [d10721s0p0].
Electromagnetic form factors and radiative corrections, including phenomenological two-photon exchange corrections, enter precision determinations and carry fit uncertainties [d4293s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do differences among experiments or analysis methods create tensions or ambiguities in combined B→μμ constraints?
sub_answers.text:
Measured branching fractions and lepton-universality ratios can differ among experiments and analyses, producing tensions that depend on experimental systematics and analysis choices [d122078s0p0].
Compatibility with Standard Model predictions can vary by multiple standard deviations depending on the theoretical model assumptions used for comparison [d125855s0p0].
Differences in input proton PDFs and related uncertainties used in experimental acceptance and normalization can affect cross-experiment comparisons [d35598s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What model-dependent assumptions (e.g., effective operator basis, lepton-flavor universality) lead to ambiguous theoretical interpretations?
sub_answers.text:
Tests of lepton-flavor universality rely explicitly on the assumption that muon and electron channels probe the same underlying rates, i.e. lepton-flavor universality [d122078s0p0].
Interpretations of branching fractions depend on theoretical-model choices and assumptions about the effective operator basis and short-distance coefficients used to map observables to underlying couplings [d125855s0p0].
Hadronic inputs such as decay constants and form factors introduce model dependence into the translation from measured rates to fundamental parameters [d10721s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What constraints do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on the Wilson coefficients in the effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ transitions?
How have ATLAS results influenced global fits of flavor observables addressing lepton-flavor universality or scalar/pseudoscalar couplings?
sub_answers.text:
Models with a light Z′ can generate the observed b→sℓ⁺ℓ⁻ effects while predicting a V−A quark current structure in the effective operators [d37511s0p0].
Scalar leptoquark models can accommodate b→sμ⁺μ⁻ anomalies and muon g−2 while being constrained by limits on lepton-flavor violation [d71088s0p0].
Vector-like fermion plus scalar leptoquark frameworks are used to link dark matter and flavor anomalies and are constrained by b→sℓℓ branching-ratio and angular-observable fits [d72444s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which classes of new-physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, Z′, leptoquarks) are constrained by the ATLAS B→μμ branching fraction measurements?
sub_answers.text:
Scalar and vector leptoquark scenarios are constrained by ATLAS measurements and searches that target muon-plus-jet final states and dilepton-plus-jet signatures [d10022s0p0,d69058s0p0].
Light Z′ models that produce b→sℓ⁺ℓ⁻ via penguin diagrams are constrained by di-muon resonance searches at ATLAS and CMS [d37511s0p0].
Models with vector-like fermions that mix with Standard Model fermions are constrained by combined flavor and collider observables including rare B decays [d60942s0p0,d72444s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are ATLAS B→μμ limits incorporated into combined experimental averages (e.g., by HFAG or PDG) used for model exclusion?
What projected improvements in sensitivity would strengthen constraints on flavor-violating couplings from future ATLAS datasets?
sub_answers.text:
Higher integrated luminosity and the High-Luminosity LHC configuration will raise muon rates but can be handled with detector upgrades to preserve sensitivity to rare decays [d121223s0p0].
Improved di-muon resonance searches at ATLAS will increase sensitivity to light Z′ and leptoquark scenarios and could discover or further exclude such models in future datasets [d37511s0p0,d69058s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What branching ratio for B_s0 → μ+μ− did the ATLAS collaboration report and in which publication/year?
What branching ratio or upper limit for B0 → μ+μ− did ATLAS report and in which dataset or year?
What are the statistical and systematic uncertainties quoted by ATLAS for these branching ratio measurements?
Which datasets (integrated luminosity, collision energy) and triggers did ATLAS use for the rare B→μμ analyses?
What significance or confidence level did ATLAS report for the observation or exclusion of B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− decays?
What muon identification and reconstruction algorithms does ATLAS employ for low-rate B→μμ decays?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS has developed small-diameter Muon Drift Tube (sMDT) chambers to increase acceptance for precision muon momentum measurement and for triggering in high-rate environments [d36328s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What event selection criteria and multivariate classifiers did ATLAS use to separate signal from background in B→μμ searches?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS event selections for muon final states include opposite-sign muon pairs in dilepton resonance searches [d48617s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does ATLAS model and estimate combinatorial and peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− analyses?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS benchmarks Monte Carlo simulations against experimental muon-rate measurements to model and constrain backgrounds from long-range muons [d121223s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What fitting procedures and likelihood functions does ATLAS use to extract yields and branching fractions for B→μμ?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS extracts signal cross-sections and yields using profile likelihood fits to signal and control regions [d98527s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are detector acceptance, efficiency, and trigger corrections determined and validated in ATLAS B→μμ measurements?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS increases detector acceptance and improves muon momentum resolution by deploying sMDT chambers to enable three-point muon track measurements [d36328s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which ATLAS detector-related and analysis-related systematic errors (e.g., muon reconstruction efficiency, trigger efficiency, background modeling, lifetime acceptance, mass scale/resolution) contribute most to the uncertainty on the measured Bs0→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching fractions in ATLAS papers and conference notes?

Quantify how uncertainties in production fractions and fragmentation parameters (for example fs/fd, bb̄ production cross-section, fragmentation functions used in Monte Carlo, and B-hadron kinematic distributions) propagate into ATLAS determinations of Bs and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios and their quoted errors.

List the external theoretical inputs and numerical values ATLAS uses when converting observed yields to branching fractions (e.g., decay constants fBs and fB, lifetimes, CKM elements, short-distance Wilson coefficients, QED radiative corrections) and state the size of each input’s uncertainty and how it shifts the inferred branching ratios.

Which differences in selection, background subtraction, normalization channels, treatment of peaking backgrounds, lifetime acceptance corrections, and statistical methodology between ATLAS and other experiments (CMS, LHCb) produce the largest discrepancies when comparing or combining Bs/B0→μ+μ− results?

Identify specific model assumptions that change the theoretical interpretation of the measured Bs/B0→μ+μ− rates (for example: choice of effective operator basis and scaling of scalar/pseudoscalar vs axial-vector operators, assumptions about lepton-flavor universality, presence of new CP-violating phases, or use of SM vs SMEFT matching) and explain how each assumption leads to alternate fitted values or limits on new-physics parameters.

Which numerical bounds on specific Wilson coefficients (e.g., C9, C10, C9′, C10′, C_S, C_P and their complex phases) follow from ATLAS measurements of Bs0 → μ+μ− branching fraction and effective lifetime, and how do those bounds compare to SM uncertainties?
sub_answers.text:
The combined CMS and LHCb measurement produced the first observation of B^0_s→μ^+μ^− with significance >6σ and reported a branching fraction measurement that is statistically compatible with the Standard Model, thereby imposing stringent constraints on many BSM scenarios [d25198s0p0].
Models with modified semileptonic Wilson coefficients C9 and C10 are explicitly targeted by predictive Z' constructions with tree-level flavour-changing down-quark couplings, tying new-physics contributions to C9 and C10 (and their lepton-dependent variants) to the gauge structure of the model [d33134s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what way have ATLAS Bs0→μ+μ− and related b→sℓℓ results altered the outcome of global phenomenological fits testing lepton-flavor universality (e.g., RK, RK*) or nonzero scalar/pseudoscalar Wilson coefficients, and which fit groups or pubblications report these shifts?
sub_answers.text:
The combined B^0_s→μ^+μ^− branching-fraction measurement is reported as statistically compatible with the SM and is stated to impose stringent constraints on several theories beyond the SM, affecting global fits that test for nonzero scalar or pseudoscalar contributions and lepton-flavor nonuniversality [d25198s0p0].
Independent tests of lepton-flavour universality in b→sℓℓ, such as R_{K^{*0}} at high q^2, have measured values consistent with the Standard Model and provide precise inputs for global phenomenological fits of LFU [d122078s0p0].
Predictive non-universal Z' models map directly onto shifts in C9 and C10 and thus provide concrete correlated targets for global-fit shifts arising from the B(s)→μ^+μ^− and b→sℓℓ dataset [d33134s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For concrete beyond‑SM scenarios (specific MSSM parameter regions, representative Z′ bosons with given couplings, benchmark leptoquark multiplets), what ranges of model parameters are excluded or disfavored by the ATLAS measurements of B(s)→μ+μ− branching ratios and effective lifetimes?
sub_answers.text:
A class of non-universal Z' models with tree-level flavour-changing neutral currents in the down-quark sector is defined and is stated to be particularly predictive, allowing these models to address observed deviations and to generate correlated contributions to C9 and C10 that can be tested in b→sℓℓ transitions [d33134s0p0].
The combined CMS and LHCb B^0_s→μ^+μ^− measurements place stringent constraints on several BSM theories, thereby excluding or disfavouring parameter regions of models that would produce large deviations in the branching fraction [d25198s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do ATLAS upper limits and measured values for B(s)→μ+μ− enter into the procedure of combined experimental averages (for example HFAG/HFLAV combination methods or PDG fits): what weights, likelihood inputs, treatment of correlated systematics, and resulting averaged values are used for model-exclusion studies?

Quantitatively, which future ATLAS improvements—integrated luminosity scenarios, detector upgrades (better muon momentum resolution, vertexing), analysis techniques (multivariate selection, time-dependent amplitude fits)—would reduce uncertainties on Bs0→μ+μ− branching fraction/effective lifetime and thereby tighten limits on flavor‑violating Wilson coefficients or coupling constants, and by how much in representative projections?
Which branching fraction value for the decay B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− did the ATLAS Collaboration publish, and in which paper (journal or preprint) and publication year was that value reported?

What branching fraction or 95% (or stated) upper limit for the decay B^0 → μ^+μ^− did ATLAS present, and which specific dataset or data-taking year (e.g., Run 1, Run 2, integrated luminosity period) was that result based on?

For the ATLAS results on B_s^0 and B^0 → μ^+μ^−, what numerical values were quoted separately for the statistical uncertainty and the systematic uncertainty (and their signs if asymmetric) on the branching-fraction measurements or limits?

Precisely which ATLAS datasets were analyzed for the rare B → μμ searches — give the integrated luminosities and proton–proton collision center-of-mass energies used (e.g., 7, 8, 13 TeV), and state the main triggers or trigger selections cited in the ATLAS papers for selecting B→μμ candidates?

What statistical significance (e.g., number of sigma) or confidence level (e.g., 90%/95% CL) did ATLAS report for the evidence, observation, or exclusion of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and of B^0 → μ^+μ^− in their publications, and how was that significance defined (e.g., local/global, asymptotic, CLs)?

Which specific muon reconstruction chains, identification working points, track-refit strategies, and dedicated low-momentum/low-rate muon algorithms has the ATLAS collaboration reported using when reconstructing muons for rare B → μμ decay analyses?

What precise event preselection cuts, vertex-quality requirements, isolation variables, and multivariate classifiers (e.g., BDT, neural net) — including their input variable lists and training samples — has ATLAS applied to discriminate B → μμ signal candidates from continuum and partially reconstructed backgrounds?

What methods has ATLAS used to characterize and quantify the combinatorial background and peaking (physics) backgrounds in B0_s and B0 → μ+μ− searches — for example sideband extrapolation, mass-shape templates from simulated rare decays, misidentification rate measurements, or control-channel normalization — and how are their uncertainties propagated?

What types of signal and background likelihood models and fit strategies (binned vs. unbinned fits, simultaneous fits across categories, use of extended likelihoods), parameterizations of mass and lifetime shapes, and treatment of systematic/nuisance parameters does ATLAS employ to extract signal yields and convert them into branching-fraction measurements?

Which procedures has ATLAS used to compute and validate acceptance, reconstruction and selection efficiencies, and trigger efficiency corrections for B → μμ (for example MC-based acceptances, data-driven tag-and-probe scale factors from J/ψ or Υ control samples, reweighting in kinematics or pileup), and what cross-checks or closure tests were reported to validate those corrections?

Which experimental sources of systematic error does the ATLAS collaboration list as largest contributors to the uncertainty on the measured branching fractions for B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− (for example: muon ID/trigger efficiencies, background modelling, mass-scale calibration, normalization channel uncertainties), and what are their reported magnitudes?

In ATLAS publications and supporting notes, how are uncertainties in b-hadron production fractions (f_s/f_d) and fragmentation functions treated when converting observed yields into B→μ+μ− branching ratios, and what quantitative impact do those inputs have on the final branching-ratio errors?

Which lattice-QCD inputs, decay constants (f_Bs, f_Bd), CKM elements, and other theoretical parameters (and their quoted uncertainties) are used by ATLAS or in common phenomenology to translate measured rates of B_s0/B0 → μ+μ− into constraints on theory, and how large is each parameter’s contribution to the total theory uncertainty?

What discrepancies or method-dependent differences (choice of normalization channel, background subtraction technique, multivariate selection, treatment of peaking backgrounds, or likelihood construction) have been documented between ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb (or within ATLAS analyses) that produce inconsistent or hard-to-combine B→μ+μ− results?

Which specific theoretical assumptions — such as the chosen effective Hamiltonian/operator basis, assumed lepton-flavor universality, treatment of scalar/pseudoscalar Wilson coefficients, or assumptions about CP phases — lead to alternate interpretations of the same B→μ+μ− measurements and introduce model-dependent ambiguities?
sub_answers.text:
Lepton-flavour universality is an assumption that is explicitly tested in B0 -> K*0 ℓ+ℓ- decays when comparing muon and electron channels [d122078s0p0].
Interpretation of measured branching fractions depends on theoretical model assumptions, and consistency with the Standard Model for B± -> π± μ+ μ- varies between 1.4σ and 3.8σ depending on the model assumptions used [d125855s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which limits on the short-distance Wilson coefficients C9, C10 and the scalar/pseudoscalar coefficients (CS, CP and their primed counterparts) follow quantitatively from the ATLAS measurement of B_s0 → μ+μ− branching ratio and effective lifetime, and how do those limits compare to constraints from B_s mixing and radiative b→sγ observables?
sub_answers.text:
Combined CDF and D0 results exclude BR(B_s->mu+mu-) > 1.5x10^-7 at 95% confidence level [d141426s0p0].
Vector-like quark models can produce values of B->X_s gamma within experimental bounds while allowing the B_s^0-\bar B_s^0 mixing parameter to differ substantially from the Standard Model prediction, thereby providing a complementary constraint to rare-B branching-ratio limits [d142043s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In published global fits that test lepton-flavor universality and scalar/pseudoscalar new physics (for example fits by Flavio, UTFit, or Caprini–Feldmann groups), how did inclusion of ATLAS B_s→μ+μ− results shift best-fit values and confidence regions for combinations like C9μ−C9e, C10μ, and CS−CP?

For representative new-physics frameworks (minimal supersymmetric models with large tanβ, generic Z′ models coupling to left-handed b→s currents, and scalar/vector leptoquark scenarios affecting b→sμ+μ−), what parameter ranges (mass limits, coupling strengths, tanβ combinations) are excluded or tightened specifically by the ATLAS B_s→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching-fraction measurements?
sub_answers.text:
In the vector-like quark model, contributions from the new quarks can account for any value of the radiative decay branching ratio within existing experimental bounds, and the same model can produce sizable deviations in B_s^0-\bar B_s^0 mixing [d142043s0p0].
Model-independent studies of B and B_c decays with an emitted light invisible boson set upper limits on related branching fractions at the level of 10^-6 to 10^-5 depending on final-state meson and boson mass, which constrains scenarios with light invisible scalars or vectors appearing in FCNC B decays [d66141s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: When groups producing world averages and global likelihoods (e.g., Heavy Flavor Averaging Group, Particle Data Group, HFLAV) incorporate ATLAS results for B_s→μ+μ−, what procedures do they use (treatment of correlated systematics, likelihood combination vs weighted averages), and how does the ATLAS input numerically alter the combined branching fraction central value and uncertainty?

Based on ATLAS upgrade plans and luminosity projections (Run 3, HL-LHC), what are the expected improvements in the B_s→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching ratio uncertainties and sensitivity to effective couplings, and what reductions in allowed parameter space for flavor-violating Wilson coefficients or specific model couplings are predicted?
Give the value ATLAS published for the branching fraction of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^−, and cite the paper (journal/conference note) and publication year where that number appears.
Report the branching fraction measurement or the 95% (or stated) upper limit ATLAS set for B^0 → μ^+μ^−, and indicate which dataset or data-taking year (or combined years) that result is based on.

List the numerical statistical and systematic uncertainties ATLAS assigned to the B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− branching ratio results (separately), including whether uncertainties are given as asymmetric errors or as separate components.

Specify the ATLAS datasets used in the rare B→μ^+μ^− searches: state the integrated luminosity (fb^−1), the proton–proton collision centre‑of‑mass energy(s) (TeV), the data-taking years included, and the trigger and selection streams used to collect the candidate events.

State the significance levels, p-values, or confidence intervals ATLAS reported for either the observation, evidence, or exclusion of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− decays (e.g. sigma significance, 95% CL limits), and indicate which number corresponds to which decay.

Which ATLAS muon reconstruction and identification strategies, software releases, and combined spectrometer/inner-detector algorithms are applied when reconstructing low-rate B→μ+μ− candidate tracks, including any tuned selections for low-pT or displaced muons?
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS reconstructs muon tracks using a precision muon spectrometer composed of precision tracking and trigger chambers embedded in a 2T magnetic field generated by three large air-core superconducting toroids [d12480s0p0].
The muon spectrometer precision detectors provide about 50 micron tracking resolution to a pseudo-rapidity of 2.7 and are complemented by an optical monitoring system that measures detector positions with 40 micron precision [d12480s0p0].
Inner tracking is provided by a silicon pixel detector with approximately 80 million readout channels that gives high-acceptance, high-resolution tracking for charged tracks including low-pT and displaced tracks [d6341s0p0].
ATLAS uses Monitored Drift Tube (MDT) chambers and upgraded small-diameter Muon Drift Tube (sMDT) chambers to provide high-precision muon position measurements and increased rate capability for improved momentum measurement and triggering [d31941s0p0][d36328s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which specific offline selection cuts, kinematic variables, isolation requirements, and multivariate classifiers (e.g., BDT input variables, training samples, hyperparameters) did ATLAS deploy to discriminate B→μ+μ− signal from continuum and hadronic-background events?
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS measures muon transverse momentum over a range starting at about 4 GeV in inclusive muon cross-section analyses, providing kinematic reach relevant for low-pT muon selections [d12991s0p0].
The muon spectrometer momentum resolution is approximately 4% at 100 GeV/c rising to about 10% at 1 TeV/c, which constrains selection performance and mass resolution for dimuon analyses [d12480s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What methods did ATLAS use to characterize combinatorial background and peaking backgrounds (e.g., B→hh mis-ID, semileptonic decays), including control samples, data-driven misidentification rate measurements, and MC-based templates for B0 and Bs0 → μ+μ− searches?

What types of unbinned/binned fits, signal and background probability density functions, nuisance parameters, and likelihood constructions (profiled or Bayesian) did ATLAS employ to derive signal yields and convert them into B→μ+μ− branching fractions?

How did ATLAS determine and validate acceptance×efficiency and trigger corrections for B→μ+μ− (MC tuning, tag-and-probe studies, scale factors, systematic uncertainty evaluation, and cross-checks with control channels like B+→J/ψK+)?
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS calibrates and validates the muon spectrometer performance through dedicated calibration and performance studies that demonstrate the spectrometer can achieve its designed momentum resolution and spatial precision [d12480s0p0].
Precision drift-tube chamber construction and testing demonstrate single-tube and chamber-level spatial resolutions and sense-wire positioning accuracies that support reliable acceptance and efficiency estimates from tracking detectors [d31941s0p0][d31798s0p0].
Upgrades to sMDT chambers and development of fast MDT readout and reconstruction for triggering are implemented to preserve efficiency at high rates and to enable validated trigger corrections at increased luminosity [d36328s0p0][d32191s0p0].
